newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police seize murder suspect's property.
newsitem.headline: Irish police seize murder suspect's property.

text.p: Police have seized property worth 300,000 pounds ($490,000) belonging to a suspect in the murder of anti-drugs investigative reporter Veronica Guerin, Irish newspapers said on Saturday.

A High Court ruling on Friday gave police the go-ahead to sell a Dublin apartment and a house belonging to the man in what was seen as a breakthrough in efforts to seize the assets of suspected killers and crime gang bosses.
The court ordered that the proceeds should go to the State.

Guerin's murder last June -- thought to have been ordered by a drugs gang boss who feared exposure -- shocked the nation and triggered demands for a government onslaught on Dublin's criminal underworld.
One of Ireland's best known reporters, she was shot dead in by a motor-cycle pillion passenger as she halted her car at traffic lights near Dublin.
The suspect whose property has been seized has a record for armed robbery and no visible means of income since release from prison four years ago, the Irish Times reported.
It said he had an ostentatious life-style, buying property and holidaying abroad regularly. One media report said the suspect is living in the Neherlands, but another put him in the Canary Islands.
One man has already been charged with conspiring to murder Guerin. ($1=.6119 Pound)
